messages:
maya: Heads-up — got a customer escalation: p95 for /v1/generate jumped from ~240ms -> ~720ms after last runtime deploy. Happening on long-seq chat workloads (seq_len 1024+).
dan: Which deploy exactly? commit/PR? any obvious changelog?
maya: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789 merged earlier today. Title: 'Enable FlashAttention2 + SDPA as default kernels'. Commit 7b3f2c1.
joan: ugh. I ran a quick query on prod metrics: p50 stable, p95 & p99 spike. Heatmap shows tail on requests hitting model "redwood-7b-legacy" with seq_len>800.
li: Can you paste a minimal repro? I want to try locally with same env vars.
maya: Repro curl from customer:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-legacy","input":"<long chat...>","max_tokens":512}'
```
They sent logs showing per-token stepping stalling around token 300-400.
ash: infra-bot shows canary deploy rolled to 100% at 09:12 UTC. TL;DR: we flipped SDPA on globally.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout finished for runtime/stable @ 7b3f2c1.
sre: First theory: FlashAttention2 + SDPA provides faster throughput generally but for memory layout edge cases (non-batched long sequences) it picks an SDPA kernel that regresses latency. Might be kernel selection heuristic.
dan: I pulled perf traces from a repro pod:
```
# top hotspots
flash_attention::sdpa_kernel::compute  48%
attention::fallback_matmul  22%
kv_cache::write 12%
```
That sdpa kernel is microstuttering with repeated kernel launches.
li: Quick mitigation: revert kernel selection by setting env var to force legacy flash kernel on the runtime process. For example: `REDWOOD_USE_SDPA=false` or runtime config `attention.sdpa_enabled=false`.
joan: Can we do a fast rollforward: patch deployment to set `attention.sdpa_enabled=false` for stable, then canary again? If that flips back tails, we know kernel choice is cause.
maya: I'm pushing a runtime config override to 10% canary now. Patch: `kubectl patch deploy/runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"ATTENTION_SDPA_ENABLED","value":"false"}]}]}}}}'`
ash: After patch, canary (10%) p95 dropped to ~260ms within 5 min. Full rollout paused.
sre: Good signal. Next steps: 1) keep SDPA disabled by default until we land kernel-fix, 2) open follow-up PR to improve kernel selection heuristics and tests, 3) add perf regression alert to catch this earlier.
dan: On the code side, suspect change in PR 789 where `choose_kernel()` now prefers sdpa when seq_len >= 512 but doesn't check batch_size==1 case. I'll open a small patch to gate on batch_size>1.
li: Also compile flag suggestion: build an SDPA variant with `-DSDPA_LAUNCH_THRESHOLD=2048` and run nightly perf matrix for seq lengths 128/512/1024/2048.
joan: For customer comms: started thread with them, told them we rolled back kernel selection for their traffic and investigating. Please add repro snippet and timestamps to the ticket.
maya: Recording mitigation steps in incident doc: set ATTENTION_SDPA_ENABLED=false, rollback commit 7b3f2c1 if needed, temp route affected customers to dedicated pool where config is controlled.
ash: Note: this also affected a few internal eval jobs — li, can you patch eval runners to pin SDPA off for now?
li: On it. I'll patch runners and schedule a canary.
sre: Postmortem items: add unit/integration tests for kernel selection, add perf smoke to CI that runs a few sample long-seq single-batch runs, and add alert for p95 increase >2x on a model-route.
dan: opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/798 to gate sdpa on batch_size>1 and added fallback.
joan: Thanks everyone. I'll coordinate release notes and customer update. Once PR 798 is green we'll re-enable SDPA behind a feature flag and ramp slowly. :thumbsup:
maya: Closing loop: customer acknowledged reduced tails, will monitor for 24h and follow up. If no regression, we can keep default off and iterate on kernel selector.
